title: The House on Blackwell Lane
author: Barış Kısır
premise: Grief counselor Iris Marsh inherits her estranged aunt's Victorian on Blackwell Lane and moves in to heal. But the house remembers her — every floorboard knows her name — and its previous resident collected the grief of strangers behind a hundred locked doors.
short_description: Iris inherits the listening house of her aunt Edith, a grief collector.
long_description: Iris inherits the listening house of her aunt Edith, a grief collector. As she opens the locked rooms of strangers' stories, her own buried guilt surfaces — she was driving the car when her sister died. The final locked room is her own; she must enter the memory of the crash and choose to let it go.
main_characters: Iris Marsh — grief counselor, compassionate, avoidant
Edith — dead aunt, present in the house's voice
the House — a character: creaks, wallpapers, door-knobs
Danny — the neighbor boy who sees
the Listeners — recorded voices of grief-stories
